title: The HULK Smashes the Horse, Philly Keeps Pace, and the Top of the Table Turns Into a Two-Horse Race
dek: Ramon's backfield buried Sonny in the week 6 heavyweight bout, Alan's trade haul won its debut, and Mekhi finally started the right guys almost everywhere except quarterback.
body: The heavyweight bout lived up to the billing for about one quarter. Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 134.4 to 102.58 as a 67% favorite, posting the top score of the week behind the two best individual games in the league. Kenneth Walker III put up 26.9 on a 21.85 projection and Christian McCaffrey added 26.2 on 19.15, giving Brucie 53.1 points from his running backs alone. The HULK is 5-1 with 829.4 points for, a ridiculous 97.8 clear of the next-best team.

Sonny got a strong day from James Cook III, 22.8 on an 18.53 projection, but the rest of the Horse couldn't keep up, and some of the help was sitting in the barn. Bryce Young scored 19.84 on the bench, and George Pickens, fresh off the trade, added 10.3 as a reserve, while Ollie Gordon II was on bye and wisely left out of the lineup. The Horse falls to 4-2 with title odds of 11% but still holds 86% playoff odds. Sonny also dropped the Bears D/ST for the 49ers D/ST, which for a Chicago guy is either cold-blooded roster management or a cry for help, and added Jameson Williams and Pat Freiermuth while cutting Jalen Hurts and Juwan Johnson.

Meanwhile Alan just keeps winning. Team Pillbert beat Randy's The fumblers 107.06 to 85.5 as a 59% favorite, and the trade imports did the heavy lifting: Chuba Hubbard scored 18.6 and DeVonta Smith 17 in their first week in Pillbert colors, while Javonte Williams put up 12 against the manager who traded him away. That's 47.6 points from players Philly acquired in deals, in a game decided by 21.56. Five straight wins, a 5-1 record and 26% title odds, and Philly still wasn't done shopping, adding Tank Dell, Brenton Strange, Dameon Pierce and Josh Jacobs while cutting Tyreek Hill and Odell Beckham Jr.

For Randy, the losses are starting to stack up, and so are the bench points. Derrick Henry managed 4.5 on a 17.6 projection, while Trevor Lawrence scored 27.34 and Stefon Diggs 13.4 from the bench, 40.74 points of reserve production in a 21.56-point loss. The fumblers have dropped three straight and sit at 3-3, still fourth in the table, but the model gives them just 34% playoff odds, the lowest of the four teams in the 3-3 to 2-4 scrum and behind two teams with worse records. Randy also swapped the Raiders D/ST back to the Rams D/ST and cut kicker Brandon Aubrey.

Mekhi's Dawgs beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 105.6 to 83.44 as a 64% favorite, and the waiver-wire king's latest find delivered right away: Malik Nabers, added just last week, scored 22.5 on a 14.6 projection. Ashton Jeanty chipped in 13.8, though Kyren Williams went for just 8.2 on a 19.17 projection. And in a twist only fantasy football can write, Tyler Shough scored 26.96 on Kai's bench, one week after scoring -0.16 in his starting lineup. Kai won anyway, and he's 2-4 with 36% playoff odds.

Zoey's loss came down largely to Bijan Robinson, who scored 6.3 on a 21.34 projection, the biggest bust of the week. Ghostu-Spider SZN has lost two straight, sits at 2-4 and has 5% playoff odds, with the 572.5 points for that are second-lowest in the league. Z² dropped Lamar Jackson and added Jordan Love, so whatever else happens this season, the Wisconsin rookie now has a Packers quarterback on the roster.

Kaushal's Habibsters beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 100.5 to 92.72 as a 70% favorite, and the hero came straight off the wire: Habib dropped Sam Darnold for Drake Maye, who promptly scored 23.8. It was a busy week of churn for Kaushal, who also brought in Tony Pollard, Juwan Johnson and the Chiefs D/ST and cut Rico Dowdle, Keenan Allen and Rome Odunze. JMoney got huge games from Bhayshul Tuten, 22.7 on an 11.69 projection, and Isaiah Likely, 20.9, but he started Jeremiyah Love, who did not play and scored zero. He also started Denzel Boston (2) while Emeka Egbuka scored 14.3 on the bench, and that single swap would have flipped a 7.78-point loss into a win, leaving Jordan at 1-5 with 0% playoff odds.

Week 7 sets up nicely. Philly hosts Zoe at Ghostu-Spider SZN with a sixth straight win in sight, and Sonny meets Randy in a game where the Horse needs to stop a one-game skid and The fumblers need to stop a three-game one. Kai and Habib face off as 2-4 teams riding one-game win streaks, with the winner jumping right into the playoff conversation. And the HULK hosts JMoney, which on paper is the week's biggest mismatch: Brucie's title odds dipped from 55% to 50% even in a 32-point win, a sign of how much the model now respects the team tied with him at 5-1.

social.author: Buckaroo Football League
social.text: Week 6 final: No Banner only HULK 134.4, The Horse is Hea 102.58. Team Pillbert 107.06, The fumblers 85.5. Dawgs 105.6, Ghostu-Spider SZN 83.44. Habibsters 100.5, Counting or not Counting GV 92.72. No Banner only HULK and Team Pillbert lead at 5-1.

social.author: No Banner only HULK
social.text: First place secured on matchday. 💚 Players of the week: Kenneth Walker III (26.9) and Christian McCaffrey (26.2). 134.4 points, 5-1, and on to week 7.

social.author: Marcus Pell
social.text: Hubbard 18.6, Smith 17, Javonte Williams 12. Alan built a five-game win streak out of other people's rosters, and the model now has him at 26%. You can mock the churn, but the churn is 5-1.

social.author: Stable Hand Steve
social.text: Bryce Young 19.84 on the bench, Pickens 10.3 on the bench, and the HULK put up 134. Still 4-2, still 86% to make the playoffs. Randy next. Back in the saddle. 🐎

social.author: Dawg Pound Dre
social.text: Last week Shough starts and scores -0.16. This week Shough sits and scores 26.96. I don't make the rules. At least Nabers showed up and we got the W. 🐾

social.author: Bench Points Betty
social.text: Week 6 bench report: Trevor Lawrence 27.34, Tyler Shough 26.96, Bryce Young 19.84. Three managers, three benched quarterbacks, combined 74.14 points watching from the sideline.

social.author: Counting Crew Carla
social.text: Tuten 22.7, Likely 20.9, and we still lost by 7.78 because Egbuka's 14.3 was on the bench and Love didn't even play. JMoney, I'm begging, check the lineup Sunday morning. 🎺

social.author: Gridiron Gary
social.text: Habib picks up Drake Maye, Maye drops 23.8, Habibsters win. Meanwhile Randy is 3-3 in fourth place with worse playoff odds than two 2-4 teams. The model has seen the bench and it has concerns.

trade_watch.take: One week in and it already looks like the model called it: Hubbard and Smith gave Philly 35.6 points in a win, while Pickens scored 10.3 on Sonny's bench and Gordon was on bye. The Horse lost by 31.82, so this deal didn't decide that game, but it isn't aging well for Sonny yet.

Still JMoney's trade: Likely added 20.9 and now has 47.8 since the deal, and Egbuka has 28.5. The catch is that Egbuka's 14.3 sat on the bench while Boston started for 2, a swap that would have won Jordan the week.

Kai's side keeps pulling ahead: Jeanty (13.8) and Adams (5.4) helped the Dawgs win, while Jefferson was on bye. That's 48 points in Mekhi's lineup to Jefferson's 15.8 in Philly's, though Alan keeps winning games anyway.

The revenge game went to Philly: Javonte Williams scored 12 against Randy and has 54 since the trade, all in Alan's lineup. Diggs put up 13.4, but on Randy's bench, so the in-lineup gap is now 54 to 6.

Three weeks later, neither side has a single lineup point from this deal: Hubbard is now scoring for Philly, and Rashee Rice did not play again for Brucie. Turns out the real winner of this trade was Alan, who wasn't in it.

bios.1: Sonny's defending champ is 4-2 after getting run over by the HULK, with James Cook carrying the load and too many points stuck on the bench. Playoff odds remain a healthy 86%, but title odds have slid to 11%.
bios.2: Randy's team is 3-3 and holding fourth, but three straight losses and a bench that keeps outscoring the starters have dropped the playoff odds to 34%. Title odds are down to 2%, and Sonny is next.
bios.3: Jordan is 1-5 with 0% playoff odds, but the trade bundle keeps producing and Bhayshul Tuten just went off. Lineup-day decisions cost him a winnable game this week; the HULK awaits in week 7.
bios.4: Five straight wins and a 5-1 record for Alan, who has rebuilt half his lineup through trades and is now watching those imports win games. Title odds jumped to 26%, second only to the HULK, and the transaction log shows no signs of slowing down.
bios.5: Mekhi is 2-4 after a win built on Malik Nabers and the Jeanty-Adams haul, with 36% playoff odds and real momentum. If he can get the right quarterback into the lineup two weeks in a row, this team is dangerous.
bios.6: Kaushal snapped his skid with a waiver-wire Drake Maye masterpiece and sits 2-4 with 677.9 points for, fourth-most in the league. The model likes the scoring enough to give the Habibsters 41% playoff odds, the best of the teams outside the top three.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 5-1 with 829.4 points for, nearly 98 clear of anyone else, after Walker and McCaffrey ran over the Horse. The title odds sit at 50% and the playoff odds at 100%; the only thing that slipped this week was the gap over Philly.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season has hit a rough patch: two straight losses, a 2-4 record and 5% playoff odds after Bijan Robinson's 6.3-point dud. She's still swinging on the wire, adding Jordan Love, with Philly up next.
